hook_text: 24 desks. How many ways can you put them in equal rows? The answer is hiding in one list.
clip_script: Classroom in Upington, 24 desks, equal rows. Try it: 1 row of 24. 2 rows of 12. 3 rows of 8. 4 rows of 6. Try 5: four desks left over, no. Try 6: that is 4 rows of 6 turned round, already found. Stop. The factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24. Eight ways. Factors fit in exactly, and they come in pairs. Now flip it. 4 times 6 is 24, so 24 is a multiple of 4 and of 6. Multiples go up: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. Factors go down: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Same fact, two directions. Bonus: 24 biscuits and 36 sweets into identical party bags? Biggest shared factor is 12. Twelve bags, 2 biscuits and 3 sweets each, nothing left over.
visual_style: Whiteboard desks rearranging into each rectangle in turn; a factor pair ladder climbing from 1; two multiple lists with 24 and 48 lighting up.
pacing: Desk rectangles in quick succession, the flip to multiples, then the party bag bonus.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find every way to arrange 36 desks in equal rows.
